newsitem.title: UK: GUS shares drop after low-end profits.
newsitem.headline: GUS shares drop after low-end profits.

text.p: Shares in Great Universal Stores Plc dropped in pre-market trade on Thursday after the retail group posted profits at the low end of expectations coupled with a cautious trading statement, analysts said.
The stock was first quoted down 18-1/2p at 646-1/2 at 0717 GMT, in volume of 65,000 shares.

GUS, which has splashed out on a series of big acquisitions in the past year including U.S. credit information services group Experian, continues to be dogged by tough trading in its core home shopping business.
It said profits overall in the first two months of the current year were "marginally in excess" of the same period last year.
"There is not a lot to get excited about in these results," said Nick Bubb, analyst at SocGen.

"The statement that they are marginally ahead in the current year is an improvement on a year ago, but given the impact of the recent acquisitions one might have thought things would be a bit better than that.
"On the face of it, our 645 million stg estimate for the current year looks a bit high."
GUS's underlying pre-tax profits dipped to 549.1 million stg in the year ended March 31, from 562 million stg a year before. Analysts' expectations were in a range of 547 million and 555 million stg.
The dividend of 18.0p per share had been expected at between 18.0p and 18.2p.
